\section[a denúncia]{a denúncia — the tip-off, the report to the police}

\label{lesson:PT-C297-denuncia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the prisoner, then the Portuguese for the cell.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a denúncia}
\textbf{a denúncia} — \textquotedblleft{}the tip-off, the report to the police\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A polícia recebeu uma denúncia anónima.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police received an anonymous tip-off.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Fazer uma denúncia} — to report someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{denúncia} is a learned word built on Latin \emph{dēnūntiāre} \textquotedblleft{}to announce, to give notice\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{nūntius} \textquotedblleft{}a messenger\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a denúncia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a denúncia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a denúncia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the prisoner, then the Portuguese for the cell, then say \emph{a denúncia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a denúncia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The tip-off, the report to the police\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o depoimento]{o depoimento — the statement (to police or court), the deposition}

\label{lesson:PT-C297-depoimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the cell, then the Portuguese for the tip-off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o depoimento}
\textbf{o depoimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the statement (to police or court), the deposition\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O depoimento da vítima foi muito importante.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The victim’s statement was very important.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Prestar depoimento} — to give a statement.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{depoimento} is built on \emph{depor} \textquotedblleft{}to testify, to put down\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{dēpōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to put down\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{pōnere} \textquotedblleft{}to place\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o testemunho]{o testemunho — the testimony, the evidence of a witness}

\label{lesson:PT-C297-testemunho}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the tip-off, then the Portuguese for the statement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o testemunho}
\textbf{o testemunho} — \textquotedblleft{}the testimony, the evidence of a witness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O testemunho dela ajudou o juiz.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Her testimony helped the judge.}
\end{quote}

Also any proof: \emph{um testemunho de amizade}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{testemunho} comes from Latin \emph{testimōnium} \textquotedblleft{}testimony\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}a witness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[condenar]{condenar — to sentence, to condemn}

\label{lesson:PT-C297-condenar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the statement, then the Portuguese for the testimony.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: condenar}
\textbf{condenar} — \textquotedblleft{}to sentence, to condemn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O juiz condenou o homem a três anos de cadeia.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The judge sentenced the man to three years in jail.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Condenar a} + the punishment.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{condenar} comes from Latin \emph{condemnāre} \textquotedblleft{}to sentence, to condemn\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{damnāre}, from \emph{damnum} \textquotedblleft{}loss, harm\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{condenar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{condenar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{condenar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the statement, then the Portuguese for the testimony, then say \emph{condenar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[absolver]{absolver — to acquit; to absolve}

\label{lesson:PT-C297-absolver}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the testimony, then the Portuguese for to sentence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: absolver}
\textbf{absolver} — \textquotedblleft{}to acquit; to absolve\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O tribunal absolveu a mulher.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The court acquitted the woman.}
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{condenar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{absolver} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{absolvere} \textquotedblleft{}to loosen, to set free\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{solvere} \textquotedblleft{}to loosen\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{absolver}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{absolver}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the testimony, then the Portuguese for to sentence, then say \emph{absolver} again
\end{itemize}
